title: City of Stars - 47 Tucanae (WFPC-2 Image)
caption: Stars near the centre of the globular cluster 47 Tucanae, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: 47 Tuc, NGC 104 · constellation Tucana · about 15000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: Ron Gilliland ( Space Telescope Science Institute) and NASA/ESA

recognition.text: Published in the ESA/Hubble image archive. No published rating.

story: Hubble zooms in on 35 000 stars swarming close to the central region of the globular cluster 47 Tucanae. The stars here are packed together far more tightly than the Sun and its nearest stellar neighbours.

The picture, taken with the Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2, shows the stars in their natural colours, and those colours carry information about each star's make-up and age. Red stars here are bright red giants approaching the ends of their lives, while the more numerous yellow ones resemble the Sun, which is in middle age.
That makes the picture more than a pretty view. By reading the colours of so many individual stars at once, scientists can learn about the make-up and age of the cluster's population.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (1.80 x 1.84 arcminutes) and distance (15000 light years), the frame spans roughly 7.9 × 8 light-years. Its light set out about 15,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2 imaged the stars through ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared filters, and ESA/Hubble describes the result as showing the stars' natural colours. The source does not publish the exact colour assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Part of the data is ultraviolet and near-infrared light, which the eye cannot see.
